Definition: from a primary κάρ (the hair of the head); a horn (literally or figuratively):--horn.
BiblicalUsage: Keras means a horn, the sign of strength and power: Luke 1:69 says God hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David. Revelation 5:6 shows the Lamb as it had been slain, having seven horns and seven eyes. Revelation 9:13 hears a voice from the four horns of the golden altar. Revelation 12:3 shows a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the horn is strength with a direction: the dragon's horns are power for evil, and the Lamb's seven horns are power for salvation. I hold that the horn raised up in David's house is the one that saves, because it belongs to the Lamb who was slain.
RelatedPeople: Jesus; King David; John the Apostle
